trust_boundaries: endpoint-to-ad: workstation/admin_ws to dc01 and adcs enrollment_svc
pki-dmz-to-pki-internal: enrollment_svc to issuing_ca via ADCS server
on-prem-to-hybrid-bridge: dc01 to aad_connect/hybrid_agent/federation_proxy (password hash sync + token claims)
cloud-identity-to-pam: conditional_access to pam_vault (privileged access gate)
architecture_summary.operational_context: Hybrid on-premises Active Directory with ADCS PKI, Azure AD Connect sync, Entra ID cloud identity, PAM vault, and federated MFA — typical large enterprise identity plane

threat_actors.name: External Attacker — Certificate Abuse
threat_actors.motivation: Obtain a domain administrator certificate via ESC misconfiguration to achieve persistent, credential-free domain access
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Network access to web enrollment service, then ESC1/ESC4/ESC8 certificate template abuse
non_capabilities: No initial domain credentials — starts unauthenticated
No physical access to CA hardware security modules or Root CA
No direct access to NTDS or dc01 without lateral movement through a compromised endpoint
No Azure/Entra ID tenant admin credentials at entry

threat_actors.name: Compromised Domain Account
threat_actors.motivation: Escalate from low-privileged domain user to domain admin via Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, or Golden Ticket from NTDS dump
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phished or credential-stuffed standard domain user account on workstation
non_capabilities: No admin rights on domain controllers at entry
No ADCS enrollment agent rights by default
No access to PAM vault without conditional access approval

threat_actors.name: Rogue Sync Agent — Hybrid Bridge Abuse
threat_actors.motivation: Intercept password hash sync or forge SAML tokens via federation proxy compromise to gain cloud-side admin access
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromise of aad_connect or federation_proxy service account on the hybrid bridge
non_capabilities: No direct access to Entra ID without passing through MFA gateway
No ability to modify Entra ID conditional access policies without tenant admin rights
No PAM vault access without valid MFA challenge

attack_paths.entry_point: ESC1 misconfigured certificate template — low-privilege user requests certificate for arbitrary SAN (domain admin UPN)
attack_paths.impact: Attacker obtains certificate authenticating as domain admin — credential-free persistence against Kerberos
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: ESC1-ESC8 misconfigurations are extremely common in enterprise ADCS deployments; enrollment service is often network-accessible

attack_paths.entry_point: NTDS dump via DC sync (AP-003 prerequisite) extracts krbtgt hash — enables Golden Ticket forging
attack_paths.impact: Unlimited domain persistence — attacker forges Kerberos tickets for any account without password
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires DC sync rights (domain admin equivalent); once achieved, Golden Ticket grants indefinite access even after password resets

attack_paths.entry_point: DC sync attack from compromised domain admin account — replicates NTDS.dit contents remotely
attack_paths.impact: All domain password hashes extracted — offline cracking exposes every domain account credential
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: DC sync is a legitimate replication operation; any account with Replicating Directory Changes All can perform it silently

attack_paths.entry_point: Domain admin account (obtained via AP-001 certificate or AP-002 Golden Ticket) modifies GPO to disable endpoint protections
attack_paths.impact: Tampers with domain-wide security policy — disables AV, audit logging, or firewall rules across all endpoints
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: GPO modification is a standard admin operation and therefore hard to detect without dedicated change monitoring

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromise of Azure AD Connect service account to dump password hashes from sync store or forge claims
attack_paths.impact: Password hash exfiltration for all synced accounts — enables Entra ID authentication for any synced identity
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: AAD Connect stores password hashes and sync credentials in clear or weakly protected local stores; well-documented attack path (AADInternals)

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromise of federation proxy service account to forge SAML assertions with arbitrary Entra ID roles
attack_paths.impact: Cloud tenant admin access — attacker controls all Entra ID resources, conditional access policies, and cloud workloads
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Federation proxy service accounts are high-value; SAML token forgery (Golden SAML) is a documented APT technique (SolarWinds)

attack_paths.entry_point: MFA bypass via SIM swap or push fatigue on compromised account — conditional access grants access without ADCS certificate
attack_paths.impact: Cloud identity compromise bypassing MFA control; PAM vault and conditional access policies exposed
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Push notification fatigue (MFA bombing) is a widely used technique; SIM swap viable for SMS-based MFA

attack_paths.entry_point: Attacker with domain admin rights disables SIEM connector service or disrupts audit log forwarding
attack_paths.impact: Blind detection — all identity events (Kerberos, certificate issuance, sync operations) stop flowing to SIEM
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires domain admin or SIEM connector service account; high impact but requires prior escalation

mitigations.control_name: ADCS template hardening — remove SAN flag, require CA manager approval for sensitive templates
Credential Access protection — enable Protected Users group, disable unconstrained delegation
DC Sync monitoring — alert on unexpected Replicating Directory Changes All usage outside scheduled sync windows
GPO change monitoring and alerting — audit all Group Policy Object modifications
Azure AD Connect service account hardening — dedicated low-privilege account, local admin removed, sync credentials in HSM
Federation proxy certificate binding and SAML token signing key rotation policy
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkey) replacing push notification MFA for privileged accounts
SIEM connector availability monitoring and audit log redundancy (secondary forwarder)

findings.severity_rationale: ESC misconfigured certificate templates allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to obtain domain admin certificates — persistent, credential-free domain compromise
Azure AD Connect service account exposure enables password hash extraction for all synced identities — cloud tenant lateral movement with no cloud-side alerting
Golden Ticket forging from NTDS dump provides unlimited domain persistence — survives password resets, persists until krbtgt double-reset
Federation proxy SAML forgery (Golden SAML) grants cloud tenant admin access — documented nation-state technique with high impact and limited on-premises visibility
MFA bypass via push fatigue or SIM swap affects all non-FIDO2 accounts; conditional access relies on MFA as primary second factor
GPO modification by compromised domain admin can disable endpoint defenses domain-wide; no automated alerting on policy changes currently
SIEM connector disruption has limited impact due to secondary forwarder; requires domain admin to execute; audit log redundancy mitigates to Low
DC sync monitoring is implemented; unauthorized sync attempts will alert within minutes; residual risk is from misconfigured alert thresholds
